doc: The Vercel AI SDK's own `ai.*` shape (its legacy OpenTelemetry integration). Its current integration emits pure `gen_ai.*` and is served by the semconv rules, including the aggregator clause that keeps a root invoke_agent span's re-listing from being read as an emission.

carriers.doc: One response, in one payload, spread across sibling keys (`ai.response.text` beside `ai.response.toolCalls`). An emission, which is what keeps a turn's intro text with the tool calls it introduces - reading it as a snapshot let the two be ordered independently and the text sorted after its own calls.
The conversation handed to the model.
The request itself: what this span was given.
The conversation inside that request, as an array that expands into one observation per message.
The arguments that tool span was handed.
The SDK's former name for its response namespace, kept because a deployed version still writes it.

detect.doc: The prefix list was a hand-written Rust matcher that duplicated the prefix dimension exactly - the clearest case that a callback was never needed. Note this identifies the SDK's *legacy* integration; its current one emits pure gen_ai.* and is attributable only by the SDK's declaration.
detect.label: VercelAISDK

messages.doc: The request, as an array of messages under either spelling of the key. Tagged with the canonical one whichever was read - this dialect reports the same carrier for both, so every span's prompt is comparable. Non-object elements are skipped: the array legitimately holds them, and emitting one produces a turn with no role and no content.

alternatives.doc: The payload is the array itself.

messages.doc: A tool call, with the tool's name and the call id from the attributes beside it. Reads a tool span, because that is the only kind of span it appears on: these spans carry no events, only attributes. The code this replaced was gated on no message having been produced yet, so any recognised event suppressed the call entirely - a loss, not a precedence.

One response written across many keys: the text here, the tool calls there, a structured object beside them, and any other member of the family swept up. Each named member accepts the current spelling and the legacy one - the SDK renamed `ai.result.*` to `ai.response.*` and both are in the wild. The role is trailing because the code being replaced inserted it last, and content identity is hashed from this payload, so the position is part of the answer.
What the tool returned, carrying the same call id so the result pairs with its call. The name is deliberately absent: the code this replaced did not attach it here.

span_facts.doc: This dialect's own spelling of the name-and-id pair.
